column3: The Hebrew leaves the initial actor unnamed; BSB supplies Abijam. It calls David his father, where BSB has “forefather”.
The Hebrew says “his son”; BSB has “a son”.
The Hebrew names Rehoboam and Jeroboam without “the houses” and says “his life” without naming Abijam; BSB supplies both qualifications.
The Hebrew actively says “they buried him”; BSB uses passive “was buried”.
The Hebrew calls Maacah his mother; BSB says “grandmother”.
The Hebrew again calls her his mother; BSB has “grandmother”.
The Hebrew describes entrusting the valuables as giving them into the servants’ hand; BSB leaves that hand image implicit.
The Hebrew calls the gift a bribe; BSB has “a gift”.
The Hebrew says Baasha dwelt in Tirzah; BSB says he withdrew to it.
The Hebrew repeats “his fathers” at the burial; BSB uses “them”.
The Hebrew explicitly repeats reigning “over Israel”; BSB leaves the second occurrence implicit.
The Hebrew leaves the initial victim unnamed and repeats Gibbethon; BSB supplies Nadab and then uses “the city”.
The Hebrew leaves the victim unnamed; BSB supplies Nadab.
The Hebrew leaves the new king unnamed and expresses the prophetic mediation as “by the hand” of the servant; BSB supplies Baasha and leaves the hand implicit.
